meta.subject: Information and Communication Technology
meta.chapterTitle: Types and components of computer systems
meta.title: Artificial intelligence

objectives: Describe artificial intelligence and give examples of tasks it can perform
Identify ways AI and robotics may help people in transport, assistance and dangerous work
Give positive and negative impacts of AI on everyday life and employment
Explain how replacing human tasks with AI may lead to dependence or loss of skills

learn.title: What is artificial intelligence?
learn.body: **Artificial intelligence (AI)** is technology that allows a machine or computer program to perform tasks needing some **intelligence**. These can include recognising information, solving problems and making decisions. AI does not always need a robot body.

learn.title: Four types of AI task
items: **Language:** understand or use words in a task
**Face recognition:** identify a person from their face
**Machine control:** help operate vehicles or other equipment
**Prediction:** examine information to estimate what may happen, such as the weather

learn.alt: Three examples of AI-related technology: a driverless transport vehicle, an assistive robotic arm and an industrial robot working away from people
learn.caption: The textbook highlights transport, assistive technology and robots carrying out risky tasks.
learn.imagePrompt: Friendly clean flat educational illustration on a light plain background in three visually separated scenes: left, a compact futuristic unbranded driverless shuttle on a road; centre, an unbranded assistive robotic prosthetic arm next to a person seated at a desk; right, an industrial robot arm welding an unbranded car body in a factory behind a simple safety barrier. Clear visual differences, realistic proportions, soft teal and amber colours. No text, captions, letters, numbers, logos, signs or brand names.

learn.title: AI can make decisions
learn.body: Some tasks need a person to **choose what to do** or **work out a solution**. AI can carry out certain parts of these tasks instead. The textbook presents this as one reason AI may change the jobs people do.

learn.title: Asimov's three laws of robotics
items: The science fiction writer **Isaac Asimov** imagined three rules for robots:
**Law 1:** a robot must not harm a human, or let a human come to harm by doing nothing
**Law 2:** a robot must obey orders given by humans
**Law 3:** a robot must protect itself — unless that breaks Law 1 or Law 2

learn.title: AI can help people, but it can also cause problems

rows.label: Safety
rows.a: A robot can carry out work that would put people in danger
rows.b: People may rely too much on machines for everyday tasks

rows.label: Quality
rows.a: AI may help improve the quality of products or services
rows.b: People may stop practising skills when a machine does the work

rows.label: Jobs
rows.a: New technical jobs may be created
rows.b: Existing jobs in manufacturing or transport may disappear

rows.label: Work roles
rows.a: Automated machines may take over difficult tasks
rows.b: Workers may find it hard to do those tasks themselves later

learn.title: AI and robots in everyday life
items: **Transport:** some vehicles can operate without a human controlling every movement
**Assistive devices:** robotics research may help people who have lost a limb or have disabilities
**Factories:** robots may perform work such as joining car body parts
**Dangerous locations:** robots can be sent to deal with explosives or very unsafe areas

learn.title: AI in transport
learn.body: The textbook shows a **driverless vehicle** as an AI example. It also mentions **driverless trains** and **aircraft autopilots** as transport technology that already automates some operations. Driverless cars are described as an area of further development.

learn.title: Helping people with disabilities
learn.body: Researchers are developing robotic equipment to **assist people with disabilities**. For example, a robotic limb may help someone who has lost part of an arm. This shows how intelligent machines may support people with daily activities.

learn.title: A robot in a dangerous place
learn.body: After an industrial accident, a rescue team finds a very unsafe area. They send a robot inside instead of sending a person. The robot can carry out a dangerous task while the team stays at a safer distance. The key advantage is **lower risk to people**.

learn.title: Three negative impacts to remember
items: **Job losses:** robots or AI systems may replace some workers, including factory and transport workers
**Dependence:** people may become unable to complete tasks without the technology
**Loss of skills:** people may forget how to do work that machines now do for them

learn.title: Give a clear impact and why it matters
learn.body: In a **give** question, one clear impact can earn one mark. In an **explain** question, link it to the situation. For example: "A robot can enter the unsafe building. This keeps the rescue workers away from danger." For a balanced answer, include both a benefit and a drawback when asked.

learn.title: AI is not just a human-shaped robot
learn.body: AI can be part of a **computer program**, a **vehicle** or a **robot**. Do not describe AI only as a machine that looks like a person. Also, do not assume AI has only positive effects. The textbook gives job losses, dependence and lost skills as possible problems.

check.prompt: Which sentence best describes artificial intelligence?
check.hint: Look for a description of what computing systems can do, rather than what they look like or how they receive power.
options: A machine or program doing tasks that need intelligence
A robot that must look like a human
A computer used only for storing files
check.explanation: AI is about completing tasks involving intelligence, such as recognising information or making decisions. A human-shaped robot is not required.

check.prompt: Tick (✓) whether each statement about artificial intelligence is true or false.
check.hint: For each claim, consider whether a program can work without a physical body and how automation affects people and workplaces.

rows.statement: AI can be used to recognise a person’s face.
rows.explanation: Recognising faces is one of the textbook’s AI examples.

rows.statement: Every AI system needs a robot body.
rows.explanation: AI can also be software that uses language or analyses information.

rows.statement: A robot can be sent to work in a place that is dangerous for people.
rows.explanation: The textbook gives bomb disposal and hazardous sites as examples.

rows.statement: AI can never lead to a worker losing a job.
rows.explanation: Some jobs may be replaced when machines take over human tasks.

check.explanation: Each two correct rows earn one mark.

check.prompt: Complete each sentence using the most suitable word from the list. Use each answer once.
check.hint: Each gap is a key word about what AI can do and how it affects people. Read the whole sentence before choosing.

items.sentence: An AI system may analyse information to make a ___ about what will happen.
Recognising people from their ___ is an example of an AI task.
Replacing workers with machines could increase ___.

check.explanation: AI can recognise faces, predict results from information and replace some jobs. The other words are distractors.

check.prompt: Match each use of AI-related robotics to the example described in the textbook.
check.hint: For each example, ask what problem the robot is solving for people.

right.text: A vehicle travels without a driver controlling each movement
A robotic device helps someone who has lost a limb
A robot handles explosives rather than a person
A student types a report with a keyboard

check.explanation: The three textbook examples are automated transport, devices for people with disabilities and robots used for dangerous jobs.

check.prompt: According to Asimov's laws of robotics, when may a robot NOT protect itself?
check.hint: Asimov's laws come in an order. Think about where the robot's own safety sits in that order.
options: When protecting itself would break the first or second law
When it is working in a factory
A robot must always protect itself
check.explanation: Law 3 says a robot protects itself only if this does not break Law 1 (do not harm humans) or Law 2 (obey humans).

practice.prompt: State three tasks that can be carried out using artificial intelligence.

markPoints.point: Using / processing language
Recognising a person’s face / facial recognition
Controlling / operating a machine or vehicle
Analysing data to predict an event / weather forecasting

practice.modelAnswer: AI can be used to understand language. It can recognise people from their faces. It can analyse information to predict the weather.
practice.explanation: State means name three different tasks. Repeating one task in different words does not earn extra marks.

practice.prompt: Give two possible benefits of using artificial intelligence in everyday life.

markPoints.point: Improved safety / robots do dangerous work instead of people
Better quality of services / products
Assistance for people with disabilities / who have lost a limb

practice.modelAnswer: AI-controlled robots can do dangerous jobs so that people face less risk. AI can help improve the quality of products and services.
practice.explanation: Give two different benefits; do not just list two different examples of the same safety benefit.

practice.prompt: Describe two different uses of AI-related robotics shown in the textbook. For each use, describe what the technology helps people do.

markPoints.point: Autonomous / driverless vehicle
The vehicle can operate without a person steering every movement / transport people automatically
reject: must be driven by a person

markPoints.point: Robotic technology for people with disabilities / people who have lost a limb
It helps them move / carry out everyday tasks using an artificial limb
Robot used for bomb disposal / welding / entering hazardous places
It performs risky work so people do not have to enter the danger area

practice.modelAnswer: A driverless vehicle uses automated control. It can travel without a person steering every movement. A robot may enter a dangerous area. This lets people remain away from the hazard.
practice.explanation: Award one mark for each valid use and one linked description of what it does. Give no more than two marks for the uses and two for their descriptions.

practice.prompt: A rescue team must check an area with dangerous radiation after an accident. Explain why it may be safer to send an AI-controlled robot instead of a person.

markPoints.point: Robot can enter / work in the radioactive danger area
Rescuers avoid exposure to harmful radiation / people stay at a safer distance

practice.modelAnswer: A robot can go into the radiation danger area. The rescue workers can stay away from the harmful radiation.
practice.explanation: The first mark is for the robot doing the dangerous task. The second is for linking it to reduced radiation exposure for the rescue team.

practice.prompt: Give three possible negative impacts of increased use of artificial intelligence.

markPoints.point: Job losses / unemployment if machines replace workers
Dependence on technology / inability to complete a task without it
Loss of skills / people forget how to do tasks carried out by machines

practice.modelAnswer: Some workers may lose their jobs when machines replace them. People may become too dependent on technology. People may lose skills they no longer practise.
practice.explanation: The textbook identifies three different drawbacks: unemployment, dependence and loss of human skills.

practice.prompt: A vehicle factory starts using AI-controlled robots. Describe two advantages and two disadvantages of this for the factory and its workers.

markPoints.point: Advantage: robots do dangerous work / welding instead of people
Advantage: AI may improve the quality of products / services
Advantage: new technical roles / jobs may be created
Disadvantage: some factory workers may lose their jobs
Disadvantage: workers may become dependent on machines
Disadvantage: workers may lose skills as robots take over tasks

practice.modelAnswer: Robots can complete dangerous factory work instead of people. AI may improve the quality of the products. Some factory employees may lose their jobs. Workers may lose skills when robots do their tasks for them.
practice.explanation: A comparison must cover both sides. Here you are asked for two advantages and two disadvantages. Give different impacts rather than repeating one.

practice.prompt: A factory has replaced a manual task with AI-controlled machinery. Explain how this could cause workers to lose skills over time.

markPoints.point: The machine carries out a task previously done by workers
Workers no longer practise that task / may forget how to do it

practice.modelAnswer: The AI-controlled machine does a task that workers used to perform. The workers may lose the skill because they no longer practise it.
practice.explanation: Explain the link: machines take over the work, so workers get less practice and may lose their ability to do it.

summary: Artificial intelligence lets machines or programs do tasks that need some intelligence.
AI tasks include language, face recognition, machine control and prediction from data.
AI-related examples include driverless transport, assistive robotics and robots doing dangerous work.
Possible benefits are improved safety, better products and services, and new technical jobs.
Possible drawbacks are job losses, dependence on technology and loss of human skills.

flashcards.back: Artificial intelligence: machines or software performing tasks that need some intelligence.

flashcards.front: Give two AI tasks from the textbook.
flashcards.back: For example, recognising faces and analysing data to predict the weather.

flashcards.front: How can AI-related robotics make dangerous work safer?
flashcards.back: A robot can do the hazardous task while people stay away from the danger.
It can replace some jobs, while new technical jobs may also be created.

flashcards.front: What does dependence on technology mean?
flashcards.back: People rely on the technology and may struggle to complete a task without it.

flashcards.front: Why can using AI lead to a loss of skills?
flashcards.back: Machines may do tasks that people no longer practise.
